module.title: Bacterial medium-chain-length PHA synthesis and mobilization
module.description: A reusable bacterial module for production and intracellular turnover of medium-chain-length poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) storage polyester. The required core begins with an externally supplied (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA pool: class II PhaC enzymes polymerize these monomers at PHA granules, and intracellular PhaZ depolymerases remobilize stored polymer. PhaG-dependent routing from de novo fatty-acid synthesis is an optional upstream submodule whose physiological chemistry is not fixed here. Beta-oxidation-derived monomer supply and phasin-mediated granule organization are adjacent processes outside the core reaction boundary.

module.notes: PhaC1 and PhaC2 are represented as members of one class II synthase family, not as sequential steps. The core module is complete from an (R)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA input boundary through polymerization and mobilization. PhaG is optional upstream context because beta-oxidation and other routes can independently provide PhaC substrates; its in vivo chemistry is deliberately not asserted as a single direct ACP:CoA reaction. The PhaG annoton therefore records a routing role without assigning substrates, products, or a module-level catalytic function. A thioesterase-plus-ligase model implicating PP_0763 remains plausible but is not promoted to a required step without direct native-context resolution. PhaC1 and PhaC2 are co-exemplars of one class II synthase role; neither is labeled primary, redundant, or substrate-specialized. PhaF, PhaI, and PhaD affect granule architecture or regulation but do not define additional reaction steps in this module.

document.description: Poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) polymerase 1 (PhaC1), a Class II PHA synthase that catalyzes polymerization of (R)-3-hydroxyalkanoyl-CoA thioesters into medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoates (mcl-PHAs, C6-C14). PhaC1 is one of two PHA synthases in P. putida KT2440 and is encoded as the first gene in the phaC1-phaZ-phaC2-phaD operon (PP_5003). PHAs accumulate as intracellular granules serving as carbon and energy storage reserves under nutrient-limiting conditions. The gene is designated phaA in the KT2440 genome annotation but referred to as phaC1 in the broader PHA literature.

review.summary: PhaC1 (PP_5003) is annotated with EC 2.3.1.- (acyltransferase) in UniProt. The enzyme catalyzes a transesterification reaction, transferring acyl groups from (R)-3-hydroxyalkanoyl-CoA donors to a growing polyester chain. GO:0016746 (acyltransferase activity) is a correct but relatively general molecular function term. The slightly more specific child term GO:0016747 (acyltransferase activity, transferring groups other than amino-acyl groups) would be more informative, since PHA synthases transfer hydroxyalkanoyl groups, not amino-acyl groups. However, no PHA-synthase-specific MF term exists in GO, so GO:0016746 is acceptable as a broad classification. The InterPro match to IPR011287 (PHA_synth_II) is correct for this Class II PHA synthase.
review.reason: The acyltransferase activity annotation is correct. PhaC1 is classified as EC 2.3.1.- and catalyzes acyl group transfer from CoA-linked substrates to polyester chains. GO:0016747 is the more informative child term for transfer of a non-amino-acyl hydroxyalkanoyl group and should replace the broad parent annotation.

review.summary: GO:0042619 (poly-hydroxybutyrate biosynthetic process) refers specifically to PHB, a short-chain-length polymer of beta-hydroxybutyrate (C4). However, P. putida KT2440 PhaC1 is a Class II PHA synthase that preferentially polymerizes medium-chain-length (mcl, C6-C14) 3-hydroxyalkanoyl-CoA substrates, producing mcl-PHAs rather than poly-hydroxybutyrate (PHB). PHB biosynthesis is the function of Class I PHA synthases such as PhaC from Cupriavidus necator. This annotation is an incorrect assignment from the InterPro2GO mapping: both IPR010941 (PhaC_N) and IPR011287 (PHA_synth_II) map to GO:0042619, but the InterPro entries cover all PHA synthases (Class I and II) while the GO term is specific to PHB. GO:0042621 is the appropriate broader poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) biosynthetic process term.
review.reason: This annotation is factually incorrect for P. putida PhaC1. The enzyme is a Class II PHA synthase that produces medium-chain-length PHAs (mcl-PHAs, C6-C14), not poly-hydroxybutyrate (PHB, C4). The GO term GO:0042619 explicitly describes PHB biosynthesis, defined as a polymer of beta-hydroxybutyrate. The InterPro2GO mapping that generates this annotation does not distinguish between Class I (PHB-producing) and Class II (mcl-PHA-producing) synthases. Replace it with the substrate-appropriate broader PHA biosynthesis term.

review.summary: PHA synthases are integral components of PHA granules. The GO term GO:0070088 (polyhydroxyalkanoate granule) description explicitly states that PHA synthase is one of the proteins associated with PHA granules. PhaC1 catalyzes the polymerization reaction at the granule surface and is physically associated with PHA granules in vivo. This is a well-established localization for Class II PHA synthases in Pseudomonas species.

document.description: phaG encodes a PhaG-family acyltransferase that connects de novo fatty-acid synthesis to medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate (mcl-PHA) biosynthesis by routing ACP-bound (R)-3-hydroxyacyl intermediates toward PHA monomer supply. Purified PhaG transfers a 3-hydroxydecanoyl group between CoA and ACP in vitro, but the directionality and exact in vivo mechanism (direct ACP:CoA transacylation versus thioester hydrolysis coupled to an acyl-CoA ligase) remain debated. Deletion genetics in KT2440 show that PhaG is a contributory but non-essential, partially redundant node in monomer supply.

review.summary: PhaG should be connected to poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) biosynthesis. It acts on ACP-bound de novo fatty-acid-synthesis intermediates and is the originally described "metabolic link" between fatty acid de novo synthesis and PHA accumulation, although the precise route to the CoA-activated PhaC substrate remains unresolved. Deletion reduces but does not abolish PHA, so this involvement is genuine but contributory.
review.reason: Complementation in KT2440 directly linked phaG to PHA synthesis from gluconate, while the reviewed UniProt entry independently places PhaG in polyhydroxyalkanoate biosynthesis. PhaG is contributory rather than indispensable because alternative monomer-supply routes remain available.

document.description: PhaZ is the intracellular medium-chain-length polyhydroxyalkanoate (mcl-PHA) depolymerase of Pseudomonas putida KT2440. It is associated with PHA granules and mobilizes stored polyester during carbon-storage turnover, with knockout strains accumulating higher and more persistent PHA levels. The KT2440 locus is PP_5004 (UniProt Q88D24); UniProt currently exposes the primary gene name as phaB, but the protein description, ESTHER family assignment, and Pseudomonas literature identify the gene product as PhaZ.

review.summary: This automated TreeGrafter annotation assigns a generic lipase substrate class that does not match the biology of PP_5004. The protein is curated in UniProt as a poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) depolymerase, and the relevant GO term already exists as GO:0050527.
review.reason: Replace the triacylglycerol-specific activity term with the dedicated PHA depolymerase term. PhaZ mobilizes intracellular mcl-PHA granules, not glycerolipids.

supported_by.supporting_text: We have demonstrated that PhaZ is an intracellular depolymerase that is located in PHA granules and that hydrolyzes specifically mcl-PHAs containing aliphatic and aromatic monomers.
